title: PHP Quick Reference
description: Look up a lesson idea, see its small example, and check a common mistake. Open the linked lesson for setup and practice steps.

entries.name: A first message
entries.summary: echo shows text. Text is a string: a row of letters inside quotes.
notes: End the echo statement with a semicolon.

entries.name: Named values
entries.summary: A variable keeps a value under a name. PHP variable names start with a dollar sign.
notes: Use $pencils every time you read that variable.

entries.name: Join pieces of text
entries.summary: The dot joins text in PHP. Joining is called concatenation.
notes: Use a dot to join text; plus is for numbers.

entries.name: Choose a message
entries.summary: if checks a rule. The >= sign means at least.
notes: Put the test inside parentheses after if.

entries.name: Store a short list
entries.summary: An array can keep values in order. Its first numbered position is zero.
notes: Position 1 is the second item, not the first.

entries.name: Visit each item
entries.summary: foreach repeats its block for every item in an array.
notes: Use the loop variable inside the block, not the whole array.

entries.name: Name a set of steps
entries.summary: A function takes an input and can return a result. return sends the answer back.

example.code:
<?php
function twice(int $n): int { return $n * 2; }
echo twice(4);

notes: Printing inside a function and returning a value are different actions.

entries.name: Look up a named value
entries.summary: An array can use text keys. A key is a label used to find a value.
notes: Use => between a key and its value.

entries.name: Check value and type
entries.summary: The === test checks both the value and its type. Text 5 is not the same type as number 5.
notes: Loose equality can convert types; === avoids that surprise.

entries.name: Choose a fallback
entries.summary: The ?? operator uses a fallback when a value is missing or null.
notes: An empty string is still a value; ?? does not replace it.

entries.name: Make JSON text
entries.summary: JSON is a text format for data. json_encode turns this small array into JSON.
notes: JSON uses quoted field names; let the tool make the text.

entries.name: Keep data in an object
entries.summary: A class is a plan for objects. Each object can have its own stored fields.

example.code:
<?php
class Badge { public string $colour = "blue"; }
$badge = new Badge();
echo $badge->colour;

notes: Use -> to read a field on an object, not array brackets.
